listing.name: Spacer Trash
listing.summary: Adds numerous unique, kitbashed ship variants to pirate and spacer encounters to keep them fresh.

description:
New Thread (Alex/David, couldn't figure out how to delete old posts)

SPACER TRASH, ver. 1.0

https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1mKh_DR7D4VNCz2nZiVW73luRbRtzlSv_?usp=drive_link

Why?

Keep Pirate encounters fresh with some variations.To show some love to the many, many sprites folks here have provided to the community. Thanks for your hard work, guys.Teaching myself how to kitbash really badly.  :-\

Lore:The Domain's collapse of hydraulic empire leaves a (minimum) fifty-year gap between the Domain and the rise of Core Power Blueprint culture. For those not lucky enough to be connected to Mayasura, Tri-Tac, or the Luddic Church, this is a time of desperate survival among planets whose economies are specifically enforced in a non-self-sufficient state... and then abandoned. 200 years on, whether or not a ship remains in service with a faction largely depends on whether blueprints have been found -- in today's Persean Sector, even known suboptimal designs will be pressed into service if there's a means by which to manufacture them.

Any old vessels without blueprints? They're just leftover trash for spacers to play with.

Mod Concepts:

There are a lot of them, so you'll see a few per game, but they're set rare enough that you won't shouldn't see every ship every playthrough.No new tech. This represents the "survival experimental" phase before certain solutions were seized upon by individual Core Powers and regularized via blueprints. Everything is an adaptation to existing tech the way Pathers and Pirates do now, and if something's a new ship, it's because pieces and parts were worked of things were put together in odd ways.Midline and High-Tech existed but the people using them are using them in Low-Tech ways. So any hull is fair game, but the goal is to "make something work" rather than to iterate progress, especially where parts of various broken things are being put together. Phase Hulls may look phasey...but they're not.Relief ships and Relics have excellent logistics and generally underwhelming firepower with an overwhelming emphasis on hammer spam and repurposed mining weaponry. Weapons are built-in as often as it makes sense to do so and draw explicitly from the most common weapons available to the survivors of the Collapse at the time. Spacer military craft run the gamut from "unremarkable" to "impressive firepower, awful logistics."Every name is meaningful: have fun, linguistic nerds.

Currently featuring a lot of ships. Some of it is blatant bloat just to keep your Pirate encounters unpredictable, some of it is ... "different." By design, none of it is intended for player use with Heavy Industry. They're unbalanced, unfair, and in some cases,

unmedicated

, which is kept in check by their rarity.

Images here bc I come from a previous century:

https://imgur.com/a/MCjw5KI

Fighting ShipsSpoiler [close]

Relief ShipsSpoiler [close]

Poverty ShipsSpoiler[close]

(there are more)

Most in-game ship descriptions can be found here(working on the rest): https://imgur.com/a/MCjw5KI. While I am pretty sure these are all safe-for-use, if it turns out I have used a ship which is not free-for-use, please let me know and I'll remove it immediately.

[/list]

aiDescription: Adds a large collection of repurposed and experimental ships that fill the gap between the Domain's collapse and the rise of Core Power blueprint culture. These vessels feature low-tech adaptations, hammer spam tactics, and repurposed mining weaponry, providing distinct character to non-Core factions without introducing new technology.

changelog.1.0:
We're now live at version 1.0.
I've bugfixed to the degree I can (should be functionally fine but may have some ships too common, will tweak pending feedback). When time allows I'll finish getting the additional ship descrips in (there's 70-odd ships, so that's a bit of work).
